terms.plain: The people running a company are usually not the people who own it, so their interests overlap without coinciding. Structural rather than dishonest.
terms.formal: The conflict of interest arising where an agent makes decisions affecting a principal's wealth while bearing different costs and receiving different benefits.

terms.plain: The amount an acquirer pays above a target's standalone value, buying control and the expectation of synergies. Certain and immediate, where the synergies are a forecast.
terms.formal: The excess of an acquisition price over the standalone market value of the target, reflecting the value of control and of anticipated synergies.

terms.plain: The system determining who makes decisions in a company and on whose behalf. In public markets largely law and disclosure; in private markets, contract.
terms.formal: The structures, rights and processes through which a company is directed and controlled, and through which providers of capital exercise oversight.

terms.plain: The majority's right to force minority holders to sell alongside it. Makes a clean sale possible, and removes your ability to stay.
terms.formal: A contractual right permitting a controlling holder to compel minority holders to sell on the same terms, subject to specified thresholds.

terms.plain: After-tax operating profit divided by the capital invested to produce it. Above the cost of capital the business creates value; below it, growth destroys value.
terms.formal: Net operating profit after tax divided by invested capital, comparable directly with WACC because both are after-tax measures.

terms.plain: Value that exists only because two businesses are combined. Cost synergies are within the acquirer's control; revenue synergies need customers to cooperate.
terms.formal: The incremental value from a combination, comprising cost, revenue and financial effects not available to either business standalone.

terms.plain: A minority investor's right to sell on the same terms when the majority sells. Protects you from being left behind with a new controlling partner you did not choose.
terms.formal: A contractual right entitling minority holders to participate pro rata in a sale by a controlling holder on equivalent terms.

terms.plain: The blended return a business must earn to satisfy everyone who funded it — the hurdle rate, and the discount rate in most valuations. Part market price, part estimate.
terms.formal: The cost of equity and after-tax cost of debt weighted by their market values, used as the discount rate for cash flows available to all capital providers.
